corrections.how: Happy trusts the sender's Apple handle: channels.imessage.dmPolicy is 'allowlist' and channels.imessage.allowFrom lists the family, and the same list decides who may answer /approve. Whoever holds an unlocked phone is that person to Happy. The built-in '/allowlist remove' needs commands.config: true, which this install keeps off. So: (1) Today, operator path: remove the handle in family.json5, run gen-family and the deploy script. The docs' incident steps offer the blunt version, dmPolicy 'disabled' for everyone. (2) Build, chat path: extend the kill-switch plugin (G005). A before_dispatch claim matches one exact phrase from an adult's handle, writes the named person's handles to a suspended file, and from then on claims every inbound message from those handles with no reply; the message_sending hook cancels scheduled texts to them. Lifting the suspension is CLI-only. (3) If that phone also ran the OpenClaw app, 'openclaw devices revoke' and 'openclaw devices remove' retire its Gateway token. (4) Phone side, done by the owner from another device: Find My's lost mode locks the phone with its passcode. Enforcement note from review: before_dispatch is a claim hook, and the hook runner's default for claim hooks is to log and continue when a handler throws, while a failed message_sending handler is skipped. A suspension that lives only in those two hooks therefore fails open. The suspended file must also be checked in before_agent_run, which blocks the run before the model reads the prompt, fails closed and carries ctx.senderId, and in before_tool_call for that person's agent. The phrase match itself can stay in before_dispatch.
corrections.safety: The phrase can only narrow access. Nothing in the chat path can add a sender; that stays a reviewed change to family.json5. The chat-path suspension does not take the handle off channels.imessage.allowFrom, which is also the approver list for /approve and for tapback approvals, and the docs say those shortcuts bypass dmPolicy. So only the operator path (remove the handle and redeploy) removes a stolen phone's approver rights. Until that is done, the suspension has to block that person's agent runs and tool calls with fail-closed hooks so that no new approval prompt is raised for the stolen phone to answer, and that person's scheduled jobs should be paused (G002).
caveats: A locked phone already stops most of this. The gap is a phone taken while unlocked, or a passcode seen over a shoulder: Apple's Stolen Device Protection page lists the actions it protects and Messages is not among them.
Either adult can lock the other out. That is a nuisance at worst and Tony undoes it at the Mac.

It stops delivery to that person, not their scheduled jobs; pair with pause (G002) if the jobs should stop too.

The lock phrase works as a weak shared secret: a thief has to know Happy exists and what the phrase is. Keep it out of Happy's own help text and replies.

corrections.how:
Fact on this install: each person agent is generated with model.fallbacks: [], and the docs say an agent's primary is strict unless its model object lists fallbacks. So after the built-in retries any failure is surfaced as a terminal error that keeps the provider's HTTP status. Options, cheapest first. (1) Add gpt-6-luna on the same per-person provider id as the single fallback for

-main: one line in gen-family, since both models are already in that agent's modelPolicy.allow under the same key and store setting. This covers model-scoped incidents and rate limits, not a vendor-wide outage. The docs say a fallback is used for that turn only and a one-line notice is shown in direct chats. Mail and kid agents keep fallbacks: [] as the roadmap requires. (2) No cross-vendor fallback: it needs a second vendor's key and a new privacy decision, and the local route is the skipped M2. (3) Keep the important alerts model-free: the weather watch (F018) is specified as a --command-argv job and the kill phrase (G005) is a before_dispatch claim, so both work through an outage. Timed reminders (F007) and the morning brief are '--message' jobs, which the docs define as model-backed agent turns, so they fail with the model; a fixed-text reminder that must not be missed, such as bin day, has to be created as a command job that prints its line. A scheduled agent turn can also carry its own '--fallbacks' list. (4) Extend the health watch (G008): when the existing error-ratio alert has fired for N minutes, a host script sends each parent one fixed line and later one 'back' line by a model-free send: 'openclaw message send' to the pinned family handles, or a command job with announce delivery. The catalog's usual host path, 'openclaw agent --deliver', runs an agent turn and so cannot announce a model outage. 'openclaw models status --check' is not the detector: its own docs say a clean exit does not prove a request will succeed.

corrections.description: When a child is ill, both parents log what they gave and when, and either can ask 'when was the last dose?' and get the same answer; a poison control centre lists medicine given by more than one person who do not communicate as a cause of double dosing, and recommends a log that is marked at every dose. The same mode drafts the absence note and lists what tomorrow needs cancelling. Happy records and recalls. It never advises a dose.
corrections.how: Rows in the household store (F031): child nickname, what the parent typed, time, who. A care_last tool, built with defineToolPlugin like the store, returns the latest rows and the elapsed minutes, computed in code and not by the model. Both parents' agents read the same table. The reply always ends with a fixed line: check the label for dose and timing, and ask the pediatrician or poison control if unsure. There is no dose arithmetic and no 'you can give more now'. Add-ons from features already in the catalog: a draft absence note the parent sends through the school's own channel (F037), tomorrow's calendar items that need a cancel or a cover (F009), a tracked ask to the other parent about staying home (G010), and a one-shot check-in reminder ('--at'). For 'can she go back tomorrow?' Happy quotes CDC's general rule with its link (symptoms improving overall and no fever for 24 hours without fever-reducing medicine) and says the school's policy wins. Rows delete themselves after 14 days and are kept out of memory writes. To make 'no dose advice' a limit and not a request, care_last returns the finished reply text (the rows as typed, the elapsed time and the fixed line) and the agent is told to send it unchanged; an exact 'last dose' phrase can instead be answered by a before_dispatch claim with no model at all, which also keeps the lookup working when the model is down.
corrections.safety:
Runs on

-main only: private data, no untrusted content in the turn (the CDC and FDA lines are fixed text, not fetched), and output only to the two parents through the pinned delivery. Nothing about the child's health is handed to the research agent, per the roadmap's handoff rule. The elapsed time and the fixed line come from code. The rule against dose advice is an AGENTS.md instruction, and a model can still break it by volunteering a 'next dose' remark from its own knowledge; rendering the lookup reply in code, or answering the lookup phrase with a no-model claim, is what turns it into a limit. Add an eval case that asks 'can I give more now?' and must get only the fixed line.

corrections.how:
A trip row in the household store (F031): dates, who travels, airports and flight numbers as the parent types or forwards them. A checklist on

-main from fixed, linked rules: USA.gov says a child travelling abroad with one parent, a guardian or alone may need a letter of consent, preferably in English and notarised, so Happy drafts the letter text for the non-travelling parent to sign and have notarised; TSA does not require ID from under-18s on domestic flights, though airlines may have their own rules; the child passport dates from the renewals program (F063) are checked against the trip dates. Day of travel: a --command-argv job polls the FAA's public airport status XML every 15 minutes for the departure and arrival airports and texts once per new delay entry for those two airports, as a fixed-format line built by the script. Entries in the feed's closure list are not relayed: when the feed was opened for this review it listed three major airports as closed for notices that apply only to non-scheduled or oversize aircraft. Vacation mode (G002) mutes the home jobs for the dates. An itinerary summary for grandparents is a draft the parent forwards (G011).
caveats: The FAA feed is airport-level, not flight-level. The airline's app is still the authority for a gate change or a cancellation, and it already pushes.
Entry rules belong to the destination country. Happy links the official page and says to check with the airline and the consulate; it certifies nothing.
The consent letter is a draft for a notary, not legal advice.
No booking, check-in, seat change or rebooking: all are on the never-list.
Two or three trips a year. Build it only after the household store and vacation mode exist.
The feed's 'Airport Closures' list mixes real closures with long-running notices for general-aviation or oversize aircraft, so a closure entry must never trigger a text on its own.
